content: 1. Doxycycline and Mestranol: Doxycycline can reduce the levels or effectiveness of mestranol by altering the intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 2. Doxycycline and Methotrexate: Doxycycline increases methotrexate levels by decreasing its elimination. Additionally, tetracyclines may reduce the intestinal absorption of methotrexate or interfere with its enterohepatic circulation by inhibiting gut flora and suppressing bacterial metabolism of the drug. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Doxycycline and Methoxsalen: The combination of doxycycline and methoxsalen may increase the toxicity of either drug due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This interaction can lead to additive photosensitizing effects. Caution and monitoring are advised. 4. Doxycycline and Mipomersen: Either drug may increase the toxicity of the other. Both drugs have the potential to elevate hepatic enzyme levels, so liver function tests (LFTs) should be monitored closely. 5. Doxycycline and Ospemifene: Doxycycline and ospemifene may increase each other's levels due to competition for plasma protein binding. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 6. Doxycycline and Pentobarbital/Phenobarbital: Both pentobarbital and phenobarbital can decrease doxycycline levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 7. Doxycycline and Piperacillin: Doxycycline reduces the effects of piperacillin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Bacteriostatic agents like doxycycline may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents like piperacillin. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 8. Doxycycline and Polycarbophil: Polycarbophil decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 9. Doxycycline and Porfimer: The combination of doxycycline and porfimer may enhance photosensitivity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 10. Doxycycline and Primidone: Primidone decreases doxycycline levels by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Doxycycline and Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Doxycycline reduces the effects of this combination by altering metabolism, while the combination decreases doxycycline levels through cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. To avoid magnesium chelation, doxycycline should be taken at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after administration of these agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Doxycycline and Sucralferric Oxyhydroxide: Sucralferric oxyhydroxide decreases doxycycline levels by drug binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Doxycycline should be taken at least 1 hour before sucralferric oxyhydroxide. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 13. Doxycycline and Trimagnesium Citrate Anhydrous: Trimagnesium citrate anhydrous decreases doxycycline levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Doxycycline and Multivalent Cation-Containing Products: Products containing multivalent cations may reduce the bioavailability of tetracyclines like doxycycline. Tetracyclines should be administered at least 2 hours before or 6 hours after magnesium-containing products. Alternatives should be used if available. 15. Doxycycline and Warfarin: Doxycycline increases the effects of warfarin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 16. Doxycycline and Zinc: Zinc decreases doxycycline levels or effects by cation binding in the gastrointestinal tract. Oral tetracycline derivatives and oral zinc salts should be administered at least 2 hours apart. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 17. Doxycycline and Antithrombin Alfa/Antithrombin III/Argatroban: Doxycycline increases the effects of these agents through pharmacodynamic synergism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 18. Doxycycline and Balsalazide: Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 19. Doxycycline and Biotin: Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 20. Doxycycline and Bivalirudin: Doxycycline increases the effects of bivalirudin through pharmacodynamic synergism. The significance of this interaction is minor or unknown.
